::: {#exm-cross-attention}

#### Three queries and five keys

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
_ = torch.manual_seed(0)
cross = nn.MultiheadAttention(embed_dim=8, num_heads=1, batch_first=True)
writer = torch.randn(1, 3, 8)
reader = torch.randn(1, 5, 8)
cross_out, cross_weights = cross(writer, reader, reader)
print(cross_out.shape, cross_weights.shape)
print(cross_weights.sum(dim=2))
```

`nn.MultiheadAttention` [@pytorch_multiheadattention] takes the queries' sequence first,
then the keys' and the values'.
Here the queries come from a sequence of 3 vectors
and the keys and values from a different sequence of 5,
so the [cross-attention](#def-cross-attention) output has one row for each of the 3 queries,
and the weights form a $3 \times 5$ matrix whose rows each sum to 1.

:::
